issues.issue: The face of the Policy promises "the full and coinplete payment of the Scheduled Payments" unconditionally and irrevocably, but the Endorsement's "Scheduled Payment" definition (c031) defers all principal to the Final Scheduled Payment Date in 2032 and c034 carves out further sums. What is guaranteed cannot be determined from this sentence once the Endorsement is read with it.

The payment timing here (the later of one Business Day after receipt of a Payment Notice or the Business Day on which Scheduled Payments are due) cannot be squared with c041 of the Endorsement, which sets the later of 12:00 noon on the first Business Day after receipt and 12:00 noon on the Payment Date to which the Deficiency Amount relates. Which timetable governs turns on the precedence clause at c064.

Subrogation "to the extent of any payment by XLCA hereunder" cannot be squared with c051, which makes any subrogation right acquired on a payment under the Policy subordinate and junior in all respects to prior indefeasible payment in full of the Owners. The two provisions give the same right different content.

XLCA is discharged once funds are deposited in the specified account whether or not they are properly applied by the Securities Administrator or claimed by an Owner, which cannot be squared with c070, by which the Securities Administrator undertakes to see the funds applied to the Deficiency Amount, or with the guarantee to Owners in c001. Whether misapplication leaves Owners with a claim on the Policy is unresolved.

This guarantee covers payments "recovered or recoverable" and is conditioned on funds not being "otherwise available in accordance with Endorsement No. 1," while c017 and c043 require that the payment actually have been returned under a final, nonappealable order before any Avoided Payment is owed. The trigger for the avoided-payment cover differs between the face of the Policy and the Endorsement.

The clause forbids endorsement or modification "without the written consent of XLCA" and names no other consenting party, leaving open whether XLCA may itself endorse or modify the Policy unilaterally. Read with c064, which gives an endorsement precedence over the Policy, the no-cancellation promise may be worth less than it appears.

The catch-all "nor against any risk other than Nonpayment and Avoided Payment" sits against the enumerated specifics that follow (prepayment, acceleration, tax-related shortfalls including interest and penalties), so the reach of the general exclusion is uncertain. The parenthetical "other than at the sole option of XLCA" also leaves unclear which of the listed items the option qualifies.

This sends undefined capitalized terms to the Endorsement, while c016 of the Endorsement sends terms undefined there on to the Indenture, which is not attached; terms actually used (Current Interest, Note Principal Balance, Extraordinary Trust Fund Expenses Cap) appear in neither instrument in the record. The chain of referral leaves core coverage terms unfixed.

The Endorsement heading gives the policy number as CA036078, while Exhibit A and the Policy itself use CA03607A. Because c054 requires every notice to "specifically refer to the number of this Policy," the discrepancy is not merely cosmetic.

The Obligor is named "GreenPoint Mortgage Funding Trust 2007-HE1" and labelled the "Issuing Entity," whereas the Sale and Servicing Agreement identifies the issuing entity as "GPMF Trust 2007-HE1" and the Policy elsewhere uses "Obligor" and "Issuing Entity" interchangeably. Which entity's obligations are insured depends on reconciling the two descriptions.

The Class A-1 and Class A-2 amounts stated here ($507,837,000 and $132,870,000) do not match the amount shown on the face page of the Policy ($13,249,000 Class A), and the series is written "2007-HEL" rather than 2007-HE1. The identity and size of the Insured Obligations is therefore stated inconsistently across the instrument.

The Beneficiary is LaSalle Bank as Securities Administrator, but the recital of the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement states that the Insurer issued the Policy "in favor of the Indenture Trustee on behalf of the Issuer and for the benefit of the Holders of the Insured Notes" — a different payee and a different class of beneficiaries. Which document identifies the true claimant is a live question.

This refers undefined terms to the Indenture, while c010 of the Policy refers them to the Endorsement, producing a two-step chain to an instrument that is not attached to the Policy. Which source supplies the meaning of a term defined differently in the two is unresolved.

"Avoided Payment" is defined here as a payment voided in an Insolvency Proceeding and actually "returned by a holder of Insured Notes as required by a final, nonappealable order," while c043 separately defines "Avoided Payment" as a payment an Owner "is required to return" following a Preference Event. The Endorsement thus contains two definitions of the same defined term with different triggers.

The final limb — "a day ... on which the jurisdiction in which the Indenture Trustee ... is located, are authorized or obligated by law or executive order to be closed" — has lost its subject, so what must be closed (banking institutions in that jurisdiction, presumably) is not stated. The grammatical breakdown changes when a claim day counts.

The Deficiency Amount turns entirely on "Current Interest," "Accrual Period" and "Note Principal Balance," none of which is defined in the Policy or the Endorsement and none of which appears in the Sale and Servicing Agreement; they are reachable only through c016's referral to an Indenture not attached. The amount payable is therefore not computable from the Policy alone.

The Final Scheduled Payment Date is fixed as "the Payment Date occurring in December 2032" without tying it to the stated maturity of the Insured Notes under the Indenture. If the Notes' final payment date differs, which date controls the principal guarantee under c031 is unclear.

"Insolvency Proceeding" reaches proceedings "by or against any Person," and "Person" in c029 is defined at large, so nothing ties the proceeding to the Issuing Entity or to any transaction party. The boundary of the term is left open.

The definition identifies the sponsor party as "EMC Mortgage Company," whereas the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement it purports to define is by and among "EMC MORTGAGE CORPORATION" as Sponsor. The misnomer puts in issue which agreement and which party the Policy's reimbursement and interest-rate references point to.

The definition first describes Insured Amounts as the portion of Scheduled Payments unpaid by reason of Nonpayment, then deems that portion "equal to the related Deficiency Amount," two measures that need not coincide. Which limb controls when the unpaid Scheduled Payment exceeds the Deficiency Amount is left unsaid.

The definition rests on "Charge-Off Amounts ... allocated to reduce the Note Principal Balance," a term nowhere defined in the Policy or Endorsement, and does not say who makes the allocation or under which provision. The building block of the principal component of coverage is undefined.

The definition uses "the Note Insurer," a term never defined in the Policy or the Endorsement, which elsewhere identify the insurer only as XLCA. Whether the two labels denote the same party, and where the term takes its meaning from, is left to the referral chain.

"Nonpayment" is the failure to receive "in full" funds legally available to pay "all or a portion of" the Scheduled Payment — a self-contradictory formulation. It is unclear whether a partial receipt is a Nonpayment of the whole or only of the shortfall.

"Owner" excludes "any of their respective affiliates," a term the Policy nowhere defines and which is not bounded by time or degree of control. A noteholder later becoming affiliated with a servicer or the Depositor may drop out of coverage without any stated test.

The enumerated list of entity types is joined by "and" rather than "or" and omits categories such as associations, estates and joint-stock companies, with no catch-all. Read literally the definition requires all listed forms at once and excludes unlisted ones.

Reimbursement Amounts carry interest "at the rate set forth in the Insurance Agreement," which is not stated here, and c051 subordinates XLCA's recovery to prior payment in full of the Owners. Whether Reimbursement Amounts are subject to that subordination or preserved by c052 is unresolved.

"Scheduled Payment" includes principal only on the Final Scheduled Payment Date (and otherwise only charge-off amounts), which cannot be squared with the face-page guarantee in c001 of "the full and complete payment of the Scheduled Payments" on the Insured Obligations. The Endorsement narrows what the Policy's operative sentence promises.

The exclusion runs to acceleration "as a result of any optional redemption, in whole or in part, or any other cause," a catch-all sitting against a single enumerated specific. Whether mandatory acceleration following an event of default falls within "any other cause" is left to construction.

"Without regard to any deceleration" appears to be a mechanical error for "acceleration"; as written the sentence tells the reader to disregard something the Policy nowhere contemplates. The correction changes what the insurer must pay after an acceleration it declines to honour.

Clause (i)'s general words "or other sum payable by the Issuing Entity by reason of any default" sit against the enumerated exclusions (ii)-(v) (Relief Act Shortfalls, Net WAC Cap Rate Carryover Amounts, prepayment interest shortfalls, taxes). How far the general catch-all extends beyond default interest and penalties is unclear.

The exclusion turns on the "Extraordinary Trust Fund Expenses Cap," a term defined nowhere in the Policy or Endorsement and absent from the Sale and Servicing Agreement, which uses only "Extraordinary Trust Fund Expenses." Whether any cap exists, and at what level, cannot be answered from the instrument.

The proviso terminates the Term by reference to "the Holders of Insured Notes," a term the Policy never defines — it defines "Owner" at c028 — while the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement defines "Holder" by referring back to the Policy, closing a circle. Who must return an Avoided Payment to trigger the proviso is therefore undetermined.

The clause fixes no deadline for delivering a Payment Notice relative to the Payment Date and does not say what makes a notice "appropriately completed" or what follows if it is not. Whether a defective notice starts the payment clock in c041 is left open.

Only two methods of presentation are listed — delivery of the original and facsimile transmission — so by implication e-mail or courier presentation is ineffective. The exclusivity of the enumerated list is not stated either way.

"As soon as reasonably practicable" and the requirement to "simultaneously confirm transmission by telephone" set no measurable standard, and the provision does not say whether either step is a condition of XLCA's duty to pay under c041. Failure to telephone could be argued to defeat a facsimile claim.

The deeming of a late-arriving Payment Notice as received at 9:00 a.m. the next Business Day cannot be squared with c055, which makes each Payment Notice "effective only upon actual receipt by XLCA." One provision constructs receipt while the other insists on the fact of it.

The Endorsement's timetable (later of noon on the first Business Day after receipt and noon on the Payment Date to which the Deficiency Amount relates) conflicts with the face of the Policy at c002 (later of one Business Day after receipt or the Business Day on which Scheduled Payments are due). The conflict must be resolved through c064.

Payment is directed to the "Policy Payments Account established pursuant to the Indenture," while c004 treats deposit in "the account specified in the Payment Notice" as discharging XLCA and c067 lets the Securities Administrator nominate the receiving account. The three provisions point to potentially different accounts.

This paragraph defines "Avoided Payment" and "Final Order" (an order whose appeal period has expired without an appeal having been filed, requiring an Owner to return a payment) in terms that differ from the definition of "Avoided Payment" already given at c017 (returned as required by a final, nonappealable order). The same defined term carries two triggers within the Endorsement.

The 2:00 p.m. next-Business-Day deadline is measured from receipt of the documents required "under clauses (x) through (z) of the preceding paragraph," but c046 conditions payment in the alternative case on further "evidence satisfactory to XLCA." Whether the deadline runs from the clause (x)-(z) documents alone is unclear.

The deemed-receipt rule for avoided-payment documents conflicts with c055, which makes deliveries to XLCA effective "only upon actual receipt." The provision also gives no rule for documents received before 10:00 a.m. on a Business Day.

Payment to the Securities Administrator in the exception case depends on "evidence satisfactory to XLCA" that the Owner has already paid the receiver or trustee, an unbounded discretion in the insurer with no standard of reasonableness. Who decides sufficiency, and on what basis, is not stated.

XLCA's waiver of any right to require the Securities Administrator to make demand or to proceed against any person before demanding payment cannot be squared with c037 and c043, which make delivery of a completed Payment Notice — and for avoided payments a Final Order and executed assignment — conditions of payment. Whether the conditions survive the waiver is the question.

The declaration that no defenses, set-offs or counterclaims available to XLCA "will be valid" sits against c056, which makes XLCA's obligations "subject to satisfaction of the conditions for making a claim under this Policy." Whether a failed condition is a barred "defense" or an unmet condition cannot be answered from either provision alone.

The express waiver of the defense of "fraud in the inducement or fact" cannot easily be squared with the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement, under which XLCA issued the Policy in reliance on the Sponsor's representations and retains remedies for their breach. Whether XLCA has surrendered fraud-based relief, or only defenses to payment under the Policy, is contestable.

Subrogation "in furtherance and not in limitation of" XLCA's equitable rights and its rights under the Indenture cannot be squared with c051, which makes any subrogation right acquired on a Policy payment subordinate in all respects to the Owners. The clause grants and the next sentence takes back.

Subordination "in all respects" of subrogation rights acquired on a Policy payment conflicts with c052, which preserves XLCA's right to seek payment in full of all Reimbursement Amounts under the Indenture or the Insurance Agreement. Whether reimbursement recoveries are caught by the subordination is unresolved.

The "notwithstanding the foregoing" carve-out for Reimbursement Amounts cannot be given full effect alongside c051's subordination of XLCA's recoveries to prior indefeasible payment in full of the Owners, since Reimbursement Amounts under c030 are largely the same sums recovered through subrogation. The priority between the two is left to construction.

Making the Policy "neither transferable nor assignable" except to a successor securities administrator cannot readily be squared with c001 and c015, which cast the guarantee as running "for the benefit of the Owners" of the Insured Obligations. Whether Owners have any enforceable right of their own turns on reading the two together.

Every notice must "specifically refer to the number of this Policy," yet the number is given inconsistently across the instrument — CA03607A on the face and in Exhibit A, CA036078 in the Endorsement heading and Exhibit B. A notice bearing one number could be said not to satisfy this requirement.

Making every Payment Notice and communication "effective only upon actual receipt by XLCA" conflicts with the deemed-receipt rules in c040 and c045, which treat notices and documents arriving after 10:00 a.m. as received at 9:00 a.m. the next Business Day. Actual and deemed receipt cannot both govern the same notice.

The obligations are called "irrevocable, primary, absolute and unconditional" in the same breath as being made "subject to satisfaction of the conditions for making a claim under this Policy." The provision contradicts itself on its face about whether the guarantee is conditional.

"A successful action or proceeding to enforce this Policy" is undefined and admits of no boundary: partial recovery, settlement, or a claim paid after suit is filed are not addressed. Whether fees follow in those cases cannot be decided from the words.

Termination "on the expiration of the Term of this Policy" depends entirely on c036, whose proviso supplies a competing termination date — when the Note Insurer has made all payments required to be made — that may fall before clauses (i)-(iii) are satisfied. Which date ends the cover is not settled by this sentence.

The Policy must be returned to XLCA on expiration of the Term, while Section 2(h) of the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement requires the Securities Administrator to surrender the Policy for cancellation "upon a retirement or other payment of the Insured Notes" — a different and potentially earlier trigger. The two surrender obligations are not aligned.

The California exclusion is expressed as operating "in the event that XLCA were to become insolvent" and cites an incompletely identified association and statute, so the circumstances in which it bites are unclear. Whether it adds anything to c060 and c061 is left open.

The precedence clause presupposes inconsistencies between the Policy and the Endorsement (as at c002/c041 and c017/c043) but does not say whether Exhibits A and B, attached behind the Endorsement, count as part of "this Endorsement" for precedence purposes. Its scope is therefore uncertain just where it is needed.

The certification rests on entitlement to demand "pursuant to Section 3.20 of the Indenture," a cross-reference to an instrument not attached to the Policy and not verifiable from the Endorsement or the Insurance and Indemnity Agreement. If the Indenture's claim provision is numbered otherwise, the form certifies to nothing.

The form lets the Securities Administrator specify the account to which the demanded amount is to be paid, while c042 directs payment to the Policy Payments Account established under the Indenture, or failing that to the Securities Administrator. The two cannot both fix the destination of the funds.

Clause (b)(i) refers to "the Insured Note Charge off Amount (as defined below)," but no such definition appears anywhere below in the Payment Notice form; the definition sits in the Endorsement instead. The internal cross-reference points at nothing.

The representation fixes the drawable amount as the sum "paid (or to be paid simultaneously with such draw on the Policy)" by the Owner, which cannot be squared with c017 and c043, under which no Avoided Payment is owed until the payment has actually been returned under a Final Order. The form permits a draw the Endorsement does not yet allow.

"Reasonable efforts" to ensure the funds are applied to the Deficiency Amount, not applied elsewhere, and properly recorded is undefined and measured against no benchmark. What the Securities Administrator must actually do before Owners lose their claim is unstated.

Here the Securities Administrator purports to assign the Owners' rights and claims, including securities-law claims, whereas Exhibit B (c080) contemplates an assignment executed by the Owner itself or by the Securities Administrator only "as Owner's attorney-in-fact." Which instrument effects the assignment, and on what authority, is unresolved.

Preserving subrogation rights "in addition to, and not in limitation of" the assignment leaves those rights unreconciled with c051, which subordinates all subrogation rights acquired on a Policy payment to the Owners' prior payment in full. The saving clause does not say which ranking applies.

"Such action and such instruments as may be reasonably required by XLCA" is open-ended, with no limit on the burden the Securities Administrator can be put to and no standard for reasonableness. The clause also leaves its own number unresolved ("[5.] or [6.]").

The appointment of XLCA as "agent and attorney-in-fact" for the Owners in "any legal proceeding in respect of the Insured Obligation" is unbounded in time and subject matter, and it is made by the Securities Administrator on the Owners' behalf without any stated source of authority. How far the power reaches is undetermined.

The general grant to "direct all matters relating to such Insolvency Proceeding" sits against the enumerated items (a)-(c) that follow, leaving unclear whether the enumeration limits the grant. "Preference Claim (as defined below)" also points forward to a definition given only later in the same sentence.

The paragraph simultaneously says XLCA "shall be subrogated to" and that the Securities Administrator "delegates and assigns" the Owners' rights "to the fullest extent permitted by law," three different mechanisms with no stated boundary. What rights in fact pass, and against what legal limit, is left open.

The Payment Notice refers undefined capitalized terms to the Indenture, yet the terms it actually uses — Deficiency Amount, Insured Note Charge-Off Amount, Avoided Payment — are defined in the Endorsement, and c010 refers Policy terms to the Endorsement rather than the Indenture. The form's referral clause points away from the definitions it depends on.

Terms in the assignment take their meanings from "the Policy including as incorporated by reference therein," which chains through c010 to the Endorsement and c016 to the Indenture. Whether "Owner" in Exhibit B bears the Endorsement's restricted meaning at c028 depends entirely on that chain.

The bracketed alternatives "[paid][or][sought to be recovered from]" are left unresolved on the face of the form, so it does not say whether the Owner must already have repaid the Avoided Payment before assigning. The assigned subject matter — "any rights or claims ... against any person" connected with the Avoided Payment — is also unbounded.

The Owner warrants the claims free only of liens or encumbrances "created or incurred by such Owner," while c002 conditions XLCA's payment on an assignment of rights and claims "free of any adverse claim" from any source. The warranty given is narrower than the condition imposed.

"The Owner ... and XLCA shall agree on such other form as is reasonably necessary" is an agreement to agree, with no fallback if they do not. It also does not say who "reasonably determines" the existing form insufficient or how a "change of law or applicable rules" is established.
